_readme: Room and furniture geometry, plus the registries that rooms.json is checked against.
anchors  — where furniture sits, as % of the room. A room can hold at most this
many containers, so adding a 7th container to a room in rooms.json
means adding a 7th anchor here first.
'rect' is for square rooms, 'soft' is pulled inward for round/hex rooms.
Keep 'soft' clear of doorZone below: a round room is small, and
furniture parked in a doorway sits under the door's own label.
kinds    — the furniture skins. Each must have a matching .k-<id> rule in
css/furniture.css. w/h override defaultSize for that kind.
floors   — the floor patterns. Each must have a matching .floor-<id> rule in css/room.css.
tokens   — the non-sortable items: keys, coins. These must NOT appear in rooms.json.
pads     — keep-out margins around furniture when scattering items, in room %.
Bigger pads = items land further from furniture.
doorZone — keep-out band in front of every door, in room %. A door paints
OVER items and eats their taps, so anything resting in a doorway
is invisible and unpickable. depth = how far into the room the
band reaches; spread = how wide along that wall.
_kindsNote: w/h are % of the room and override defaultSize for that kind.
They were a flat 36 x 7 for everything, which is why furniture read as
a labelled bar rather than an object. Give each kind the silhouette it
should have: a fridge tall and narrow, a crate wide and low.
Keep h under ~20 or the bottom row of anchors runs off the floor.
_shapeKindsNote: THE SECOND WAVE, and the reason for it: a container's skin has to agree with
its NAME. The first eleven kinds were MATERIALS (steel, wood, wicker), which
is a fine axis right up until a room holds a sink and a fridge and both of
them are `steel` — at which point the player is reading a name plate to tell
two identical grey boxes apart, and the furniture has stopped doing its job.
These twelve are SHAPES instead: a sink has a tap, a bin has a lid, a hook
rail has hooks, a heap has no straight edges at all.
The rule that came out of it: NO TWO CONTAINERS IN ONE ROOM SHARE A KIND.
validate.js warns when they do. A room is where the player is comparing
furniture, so a room is where two identical silhouettes cost something.
Same reasoning as the confusable-emoji rule in rooms.json, one layer up.
_worldKindsNote: hull / arcane / mesh were added with the ship, tower and zoo themes so a new
world is not the house's furniture in a different colour. A theme's palette
(css/themes.css) only repaints the WALLS — the furniture is drawn from these
kinds and stays whatever it was, so without a kind of its own a wizard's rune
cabinet is a chest of drawers standing in a purple room.
Each needs a .k-<id> skin in css/furniture.css; validate.js checks both ways.
_floorsNote: One id per room, and each needs a matching .floor-<id> rule in css/room.css.
Grouped by theme below purely for reading; the list itself is flat and order
_holdallNote: THE HOLDALL'S FOOTPRINT, in room %. It is furniture — see onHoldall() in
js/geometry.js — so it gets a slot like a cupboard (34x16) and a coin box
(9x4.2) do, and every placement path in the game keeps clear of it for
free. It was drawn at a fixed pixel size at first, over the floor rather
than in it, and 71% of its surface was covered by clutter you could not
move: an item lying on it swallowed the tap, and there was no keep-out to
Between a cache and a cupboard on purpose: big enough to hit with a thumb,
small enough that dropping one into every room does not eat the floor.
